keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «한때 잘 듣던 항생제가 결국 전혀 듣지 않게 될 수 있다(문제)» 와 «항생제는 소중한 도구이고, 그것을 현명하게 쓰는 것은 모두의 책임이다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the problem (an antibiotic that once worked well may stop working altogether) and the conclusion (antibiotics are precious tools, and using them wisely is everyone’s responsibility). The green sentences are the answers.

boxes.a: Surviving bacteria pass on resistance, so antibiotics may stop working
Take antibiotics exactly as directed and never share them

qs.q: Why may an antibiotic that once worked well stop working?
qs.qko: 왜 한때 잘 듣던 항생제가 더 이상 듣지 않게 될 수 있나요?
opts: Because the medicine loses its power when it gets old
Because surviving bacteria multiply and pass on their resistance
Because doctors prescribe it too carefully
evs: That mold led to penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic.
These survivors multiply and pass on their resistance.
Fleming himself warned about this danger in his Nobel Prize speech in 1945.
Meanwhile, very few new types of antibiotics have been developed in recent decades.
why: 항생제를 써도 살아남은 몇몇 세균이 수를 늘리면서 내성을 물려줘요. 그래서 시간이 지나면 약이 듣지 않게 돼요.
A few bacteria survive, then multiply and pass on their resistance, so over time the antibiotic stops working.

qs.q: In the text, what does 'bacteria are fighting back' mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 'bacteria are fighting back(세균이 반격하고 있다)' 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: Bacteria are becoming able to survive antibiotics
Bacteria are attacking doctors and scientists
Bacteria are helping antibiotics work better
evs: A mold had grown on one of them, and the bacteria around it had died.
When antibiotics are used, most bacteria die, but a few may survive because of small genetic differences.
These survivors multiply and pass on their resistance.
Still, there are reasons for hope.
why: 바로 뒤 문장들에서 몇몇 세균이 항생제를 견디고 살아남아, 수를 늘리며 내성을 물려준다고 설명해요. 세균이 약을 이겨 내는 힘을 갖게 된다는 뜻이에요.
The next sentences explain that a few bacteria survive antibiotics, multiply, and pass on their resistance. Bacteria are becoming able to survive the medicine.

qs.q: Why does the writer say human behavior has made the problem worse?
qs.qko: 글쓴이는 왜 사람들의 행동이 문제를 더 나쁘게 만들었다고 말하나요?
opts: Because people refuse to take any antibiotics at all
Because farm animals no longer receive antibiotics
Because people misuse antibiotics, for example for viral illnesses or by stopping too early
evs: Some people take antibiotics for colds and flu, even though these illnesses are caused by viruses, which antibiotics cannot kill.
Since the 1940s, they have saved millions of lives by curing infections that were once deadly, such as pneumonia and infected wounds.
Others stop taking their medicine too early, and in many countries large amounts of antibiotics are given to farm animals.
Scientists are searching for new medicines, and doctors are learning to prescribe antibiotics more carefully.
why: 어떤 사람들은 바이러스가 원인인 감기나 독감에 항생제를 먹고, 어떤 사람들은 약을 너무 일찍 끊어요. 두 문장을 함께 보면 사람들이 항생제를 잘못 쓰고 있다는 걸 알 수 있어요.
Some people take antibiotics for viral illnesses like colds, and others stop their medicine too early. Together these show that people misuse antibiotics.

ends: How did scientists turn a mold into a medicine?
How are scientists searching for new antibiotics?
과학자들은 새로운 항생제를 어떻게 찾고 있을까?

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «because» 뒤에 «누가/무엇이 + 어떻게 된다» 를 넣어 이유를 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: because germs can spread to my family)
